problem: The post-merge production readback remained in the exact-deploy wait even though Netlify production, release.json and live HTML all exposed the exact merge SHA.
rootCause: The exact release-identity polling step called the full live-site contract, which also enforced stale pricing semantics. Unrelated pricing markup drift therefore prevented deploy identity from becoming ready.
root_cause: The exact release-identity polling step called the full live-site contract, which also enforced stale pricing semantics. Unrelated pricing markup drift therefore prevented deploy identity from becoming ready.
preventionRule: Release-identity polling proves exact production SHA plus canonical shell only; pricing semantics remain fail-closed in their dedicated pricing/browser gates.
prevention: Keep exact merge SHA, production context and Netlify deploy id mandatory.
Keep the canonical shell contract mandatory during release-identity polling.
Do not couple release identity to page-specific pricing semantics.
Keep pricing semantics strict by default in the live contract.
Retain dedicated browser and pricing gates for content and interaction proof.

evaluation.expected: A valid exact production release can clear identity polling independently of pricing semantics, while the default pricing contract still fails closed when its required semantics are absent.
